labels.label: bzcor:c3s3p9c_corps_convexe_hemisphere

hypotheses.paper: A un corps convexe de S(n)

findings: No proof is printed; the anchor wraps the strict IsCorpsConvexeS.exists_forall_pos (Chapter2/Hilbert). corollaire_hemisphere_prop9 also proves it by the route the placement suggests: D(A) is a convex body (Prop. 8, isCorpsConvexeS_D), take M ∈ int D(A), then Prop. 9 puts A in the open hemisphere int D({M}).

labels.label: bzprop:c3s3p10_interieur_dual

hypotheses.note: prop10 carries both; the direct implication prop10_forward needs only A closed, B any part

findings: The printed proof (l.838–849) is not followed: its display int D(A) = ⋂_{M∈A} int D({M}) swaps interior with an infinite intersection, true here only because A is compact (it is the ← direction of mem_interior_D_iff, proved by the tube lemma), and its last step asks D(B) ⊂ D({M}) where int D({M}) is needed (the [sic?] at l.848, OQ-160 (a)). The statement is unaffected. The converse is the paper's: D ∘ D = id on C(S(n)) (dotPairing_prop1).
